title: Customer report delivery contracts & observability for scheduled exports
creator: Maya Chen
description: Stabilize scheduled customer reporting pipelines (CSV/S3 and webhook deliveries) by formalizing delivery contracts, improving backpressure handling, and adding end-to-end observability. Current incidents show delayed or duplicated deliveries when downstream consumers are slow or retry aggressively; customers need clear SLAs, manifest guarantees, and cost-predictable retries.
background: Over the past two quarters we've observed three recurring failure modes in scheduled exports: 1) silent retries that produce duplicate CSVs, 2) long tail latencies when S3 throttles cause retry storms, and 3) webhooks queuing up without clear visibility into consumer success. Existing manifests are ad-hoc and consumers have implemented brittle parsing logic. This ticket consolidates contract, retry, and observability work so that teams can rely on exports for billing, audits, and downstream pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Export manifest schema v2 published and documented (backwards-compatible transform for v1 consumers)
Scheduler emits per-tenant delivery events to metrics pipeline (success/failure/latency/retries)
S3 upload and webhook delivery implements idempotency keys and dedupe window; downstream dedupe guide published
Backpressure path: when consumer endpoints return sustained 429/5xx, system applies exponential backoff + backfill window tracked in manifest
Operational playbook and Grafana dashboards live in console-exports dashboard folder; alerting thresholds defined
End-to-end integration test that simulates slow consumer and verifies no silent duplication and bounded retry cost
technical_design: Introduce a canonical export manifest (JSON) with fields: manifest_id, tenant_id, export_range, file_locations (primary/backup), checksum, idempotency_key, attempted_deliveries, last_attempt_ts, status. Update scheduler to write the manifest to internal S3 prefix before initiating delivery. Delivery workers will consult the manifest and use a distributed lease to avoid double-sends. For webhooks, add a delivery queue with token-bucket rate limit per-consumer and an adaptive exponential-backoff state machine persisted in Redis. Metrics: instrument histograms for delivery latency, counter for deduplicated_deliveries, and a gauge for queued_per_tenant. Add tracing spans that include manifest_id and export_batch_id.
migration_plan: 1) Deploy manifest schema v2 writer alongside v1 for 2 weeks (dual-write). 2) Notify known consumer integrations of v2 with migration guide and sample parser. 3) Enable dedupe/lease logic behind feature flag and slowly ramp per-tenant (10% -> 50% -> 100%). 4) After 30 days of stable metrics, disable dual-write and mark v1 deprecated.
rollout_plan: Week 0: Feature flag off in prod, integration tests in staging
Week 1: Enable dual-write for internal tenants; validate dashboards and dedupe metrics
Week 2: Enable feature-flagged delivery logic for non-critical tenants (10% traffic)
Week 3: Ramp to 50% contingent on metric stability
Week 4: Full rollout and deprecation of v1
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Consumers fail to adopt manifest v2 -> Mitigation: maintain v1 dual-write and provide parser libraries in Python/Node
Risk: Redis lease starvation under high concurrency -> Mitigation: use sharded leases and fall back to S3-backed atomic compare-and-set for critical sections
Risk: Cost spikes due to retries -> Mitigation: cap retry budget per tenant and expose retry_cost usage metric to customers
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest writer/reader and lease semantics
Integration tests simulating slow S3 (inject 503s) and websocket consumer slow ack
Chaos test: kill delivery worker pool while exports are in-flight and verify resumability
E2E staging run with synthetic tenants and verification scripts to check dedupe and idempotency
qa_notes: QA should validate both CSV and ndjson outputs, verify checksum correctness, and simulate consumer retry patterns (immediate retry, exponential retry, flaky 50% success). Also validate dashboards show appropriate metrics and that alerts fire at configured thresholds during induced failures.
